transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Alvarez (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (SRE Lead, Solara), Elena Torres (CTO, Solara), Priya Kapoor (Security Engineer, Solara)

Auto-summary (auto):
Solara Health is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and dedicated inference with strict data residency and availability constraints. Main concerns: predictable P95 latency under burst, regional failover behavior, auditability (SOC2/ISO), KMS/HSM integration, and how Redwood does graceful degradation (fallback models, cache priming, partial results). They asked for concrete perf numbers, a Dedicated trial, and security docs.

Topics:
- Hosted vs Dedicated economics and failure modes
- Multi-region routing and regional failover sequence
- Fallback policies (model variants, cached responses, degraded output)
- Compliance: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, network isolation (VPC)
- Rollout/playbook: canaries, circuit breakers, retries, traffic steering

Action items (auto): See metadata section.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run about 45, 50 minutes, just to align on your reliability constraints and then Priya will dig into some of the infra questions, sound good?
[00:07] Elena: yep, sounds good—thanks Jordan. Quick thing, we might drop in and out, Mark has to jump to a standup at 16:30, but try to capture the perf asks.
[00:13] Mark: yea, sorry in advance.
[00:15] Jordan: no worries. So quick context, Solara — you're a healthcare platform, correct? Are you looking at hosted first or more leaning private/dedicated?
[00:22] Elena: We're hybrid. For dev and lower risk services hosted is fine. But for PHI-related inference we need dedicated or private in a VPC with our KMS, it's non-negotiable. We also have data residency — EU and US east.
[00:34] Priya Nair (SE): got it. On the network side we support private deployments with customer-managed VPC peering and H S M/K M S integrations for key material, that work for you?
[00:42] Priya Kapoor: yes we use HSMs for key attestations and require keywrap. We'll need audit logs, immutable event history for access.
[00:49] Jordan: perfect, we'll share the SOC two and ISO artifacts and our network diagram after.
[00:54] Mark: main infra question — how do you handle regional failures? If us-east goes down, what's traffic flow to EU, and how do you ensure consistent model versioning across regions?
[01:04] Priya Nair (SE): good q. We have smart routing policies: you can set primary region affinity with automatic fallback to secondary regions. Model versions are replicated as model bundles; we support pinned versions so the same model artifacts are deployed in the fallback region. There's a small lag for syncing large weights — usually minutes for our delta distribution, but can be optimized with pre-warmed replicas.
[01:21] Elena: minutes is okay in some cases but for low-latency front-door flows we need sub-500ms tail in usual case and deterministic behavior during failover. How do you avoid cold-starts or KV cache misses in the fallback?
[01:33] Priya Nair (SE): two levers — prefix / KV cache warm-up and model variant fallbacks. For critical paths we recommend either Dedicated pools in both regions or warm passive replicas. With hosted, you can enable cross-region warm replicas as part of an SLA add-on. The KV cache (we sometimes say K V cache in notes) can be primed via traffic mirroring or a scheduled priming job to keep token-level state present.
[01:52] Mark: traffic mirroring sounds heavy; can you do read-through cache or edge caching?
[01:56] Priya Nair (SE): yes, for some use-cases edge caching of prompt templates and deterministic responses is possible. For generative outputs we recommend model fallbacks — e.g., switch to a smaller quantized variant that fits on warm nodes to keep latency bounded instead of blocking.
[02:10] Jordan: also worth noting the runtime supports continuous batching so tail behavior improves with consistent QPS. But that collides with strict per-request latency SLOs sometimes.
[02:18] Elena: right — our SLO is 99.95 for critical endpoints, P95 target 120ms, P99 under 400ms. We need to map those to realistic throughput. We also budget an RTO of 5 minutes for degraded-mode responses.
[02:31] Priya Kapoor: RTO 5 minutes — meaning in the event of region outage you want some graceful degraded responses within 5 min?
[02:36] Elena: yes, we accept lower quality (e.g., truncated or simpler model) but service must return something rather than time out.
[02:42] Priya Nair (SE): makes sense. Our recommended strategy: 1) local primary with prefix/KV caching 2) health-based circuit breakers that flip to fallback model variant 3) if region unreachable then route to secondary region with pre-warmed lightweight model + cached KV state where possible 4) if even that fails, return a structured degraded response (short summary + confidence) so app can decide.
[03:01] Mark: how do fallbacks handle stateful conversations? If KV cache isn't replicated, user context will be missing. We need to avoid hallucination.
[03:09] Priya Nair (SE): that is a hard problem — you can keep key context in a distributed store that is replicated across regions (we integrate with customer-managed Redis/elasticache) or you can checkpoint conversational state to your own backend and pass to the fallback region. For some customers we recommend a hybrid: replicate last-n turns via secure sync and rely on short-term cache. We'll include the trade-offs in the write-up.
[03:28] Elena: we'll need clear notes on what 'degraded but safe' output looks like.
[03:32] Jordan: totally. Another angle — SLA. What kinds of uptime commitments do you offer for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[03:38] Priya Nair (SE): Hosted: 99.9 standard, with optional paid tiers to 99.95 depending on multi-region config. Dedicated: contractual SLA up to 99.99 with reserved pools, health probes, and scheduled pre-warm windows.
[03:50] Elena: do you bake in cross-region standby for the 99.99?
[03:53] Priya Nair (SE): yes, for 99.99 we require either active-active or active-passive with warm standby and replication. We also add runbooks and breach credits in the contract.
[04:03] Mark: curious about cost leakage — active-active doubles cost. Is Redwood able to do burstables where standby is cheaper until failover?
[04:10] Jordan: yes, we have burst-capacity options and 'warm standby' pricing where nodes are smaller or quantized to save cost and ramp up on failover, plus autoscale policies for traffic spikes. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization/batching profiles to meet your cost target while keeping latency constraints.
[04:27] Elena: you mentioned audit logs earlier — we need immutable access logs, per-token billing traces, and who-deployed events. How granular are those?
[04:36] Jordan: token-level billing and per-request traces are available in the Console. For private deployments we can ship logs to your SIEM — CloudWatch/Splunk or via syslog — and we can integrate with your KMS for key usage audit.
[04:48] Priya Kapoor: and retention? We have strict retention windows and differ by region — logs with PHI must stay in-region and have limited retention.
[04:55] Priya Nair (SE): retention is configurable; for private we support region-bound retention and encryption at rest with your keys. We'll share the dataflow diagram.
[05:02] Mark: what about chaos testing? We run sim outage tests and care about cold starts during failover — do you have recommended blast radius and circuit breaker configs?
[05:12] Priya Nair (SE): yes, we suggest staged chaos: start with single-pod termination, then AZ failure, then region failover. Circuit breaker thresholds are typically set on error rate and latency percentiles; for example 5% error rate sustained over 30s or P99 latency breaching twice the SLO for N seconds. We can provide default templates.
[05:31] Jordan: I've seen customers set degraded-mode routes for 0.5–2% of traffic as canary and escalate.
[05:38] Elena: ok, that's helpful. There's also security review — SSO/SAML, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC. We have compliance team who will need a security questionnaire.
[05:48] Jordan: we'll send SAML and SCIM docs; Priya (SE) will include recommended RBAC roles.
[05:53] Priya Kapoor: KMS integration question — do you support external HSMs or do we need to use Redwood managed KMS?
[05:59] Priya Nair (SE): for Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS/HSM via standard keywrap and kms-proxy patterns. For hosted you can bring your own keys in some enterprise plans but full HSM control typically in private installs.
[06:12] Mark: great. On model replication — you mentioned minutes to sync large weights. What's the largest model you've replicated cross-region, and what's the typical time?
[06:21] Priya Nair (SE): realistic example: a 30GB quantized model with delta-transfer can replicate in ~3–7 minutes depending on link. For multi-hundred GB families it's tens of minutes; for those we recommend warm standby or smaller fallbacks. We'll include bandwidth/replication numbers tied to infra region.
[06:37] Elena: what about runtime fallback that can serve partial tokens? E.g., in a failover scenario we want to return partial result and indicate continuity token so app can re-request remaining tokens once full model comes up.
[06:48] Priya Nair (SE): yes we support streaming partial tokens and a continuity token in the header. If you design your app to accept partial responses you can avoid timeouts. We can surface that as a contract.
[06:58] Mark: sounds useful. A tangent: for privacy we prefer not to send some patient PII to any external service — can Redwood enforce field-level redaction or do that pre-send?
[07:07] Jordan: Redwood doesn't do application-layer redaction by default, it's recommended to preprocess on your side or use request filters in the SDK. For Private deployments we can co-deploy redaction hooks.
[07:16] Elena: okay. Let's talk about testing — we want to run a Dedicated trial to measure P95 under both steady and burst traffic and validate failover behavior. What are the constraints?
[07:26] Priya Nair (SE): trial typically provisions a small Dedicated pool for 2 weeks; we recommend a test matrix: 1) steady-state load at X qps for 1 hour 2) spike tests (3x qps) for 10 minutes 3) failover simulation with region route disabled 4) cache-warm vs cold-case runs. We'll help with scripts and provide a benchmark sheet.
[07:44] Mark: can we bring our own traffic generator or do you run it?
[07:47] Priya Nair (SE): either. We can share a load harness and sink logs to your S3 or to our console.
[07:52] Jordan: I'll include a sample perf workbook and a list of config flags.
[07:56] Elena: about incident playbooks — we need an on-call handoff with Redwood for escalations. SLA includes an escalation path?
[08:03] Priya Nair (SE): yes, Dedicated customers get a P1/P2 escalation matrix and named CSM + optional 24/7 support for production-critical tiers.
[08:11] Mark: what about regional throttling during outages — do you do token-pricing adjustments or burst credits to avoid surprise bills?
[08:19] Jordan: we can provide rate-limit knobs and quota alerts and also have burst credits as a contract clause. Billing is per-token but for Dedicated we can do fixed-price reserved pools.
[08:29] Elena: good. Any known customer stories with similar healthcare constraints?
[08:32] Jordan: yes, several — one provider used warm standby with quantified fallbacks and avoided user-visible outages during two AZ failures in a year. We can anonymize references and include the case study.
[08:42] Priya Kapoor: final quick question — can Redwood prove non-repudiation for model outputs? We need chain of custody for decisions.
[08:49] Priya Nair (SE): we have request-level metadata and signed attestations for model version + weights hash; in Private you can enable signing with your keys. That gives chain of custody for which model produced an output.
[08:59] Mark: that's big for us.
[09:01] Jordan: ok I'll summarize next steps.
[09:03] Jordan: Next steps: 1) Jordan sends pricing worksheet and perf workbook 2) Priya Nair sends config templates, chaos test templates, and replication numbers 3) Solara sends traffic profiles and compliance questionnaire answers 4) schedule deep-dive week of Jan 25.
[09:18] Elena: sounds good, thanks. Mark and I will sync offline to add any other constraints.
[09:23] Mark: thanks all, gotta run.
[09:25] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs.
